correctness.rationale: The independent two-sided stationary environment yields an exactly Gaussian conditional state with H<=V<=L. Each fixed stiff interval puts the next soft-birth gap Z in a strictly positive deterministic compact interval. Stationary soft-phase age has integrated Pareto survival, giving the sharp variance-gap CDF with exponent 1-beta and coefficient c/((mu+tau)(beta-1)); the stiff-phase contribution is smaller by a logarithmic factor. The Gaussian-mixture Laplace transform of this slowly varying gap CDF yields the stated normalized spatial density equivalent, including its Gaussian and logarithmic constants. Numerical quadrature on two parameter sets validates the independent kernel bounds; the analytic argument proves the asymptotic.

value.rationale: The exact logarithmic suppression distinguishes the far tail of a permanently confining but intermittently softened trap from algebraic excursions of genuinely free-diffusion phases. It exposes a measurable residence-tail exponent in a marginal that otherwise appears Gaussian at leading exponential order, clarifies a singular physical boundary, and yields a reusable sharp asymptotic with a nontrivial coefficient.
